name: eq0hnw-canary-tracker-restart
goal: The needs-you release canary rides out a Tracker daemon restart: a command the service did not answer is repeated, so a restart does not abort a tap wait, leave a test ask open or lose the release record

evidence: Live failure 2026-11-27T12:05:18Z (deploy 0j8kry, canary-run.log): the primary tracker was SIGKILL-restarted (pid 42705 -> 98381) 15 min into the Hub web tap wait. One 'tracker show' failing with 'tracker: native service unavailable' ended the web check, its cleanup failed (test item qdynwp left open as a Daniel ask until the deploy session closed it), mac and iphone failed at 'add' without an ask, and the result note never reached the release (exit 1, release not held). Expected: a command the service did not answer is repeated for a bounded time; refusals are not repeated. Reproduction: test/needs-you-canary-restart.test.ts.

Gap: test/support/needsYouCanaryWorld.ts is an in-memory tracker that answers every command, so no canary test ever had a tracker call fail in transit. Reusable change: test/support/needsYouCanaryOutage.ts takes the error from the real native CLI (run through the canary's real trackerCli against a closed loopback port), and the new test injects it per call and over time.

loop record red at 2906f55215 (test-only commit): bunx vitest run test/needs-you-canary-restart.test.ts, 3 failed / 3 passed. The 3 failures are the live symptoms (tap wait aborted, steps lost to unanswered calls, hold not recorded); the 3 that pass are guards (real CLI message, bounded give-up, refusals not repeated).

64b0c8aa58: scripts/needs-you-canary/patientTracker.ts repeats only a command that printed 'native service unavailable', 3 s apart for up to 5 minutes; runCanary wraps its tracker in it. The spec also says what a repeated write can leave behind. Units check valid.
loop record green passed at 64b0c8aa58 with the red tests unchanged since 2906f55215 (same command, 6 tests).
